newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond bulls run amok, on RBA watch.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond bulls run amok, on RBA watch.

text.p: FUTURES CASH YIELD
*Australian bond yields ended at the lowest level since March 1994 after August quarter wages rose just 0.7 percent.
*Expectations are running high for an early easing in monetary policy with a 50 basis point rate cut fully priced in.
By Colin Brinsden

Australian bond yields fell to their lowest level since March 1994 after a combination of benign inflation and wages data over the past two days refuelled expectations of an early easing in official interest rates.
Bill futures also priced in a 50 basis point easing, and such has been the weak outcome of both sets of figures that the market will be closely watching the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) on Friday.
However, analysts looking for an early cut believe the most likely timing will be after the November 5 RBA board meeting.

"While the recent quarterly report of the Reserve Bank drew attention to the more rapid pace of enterprise bargaining settlements as opposed to today's measure of average weekly earnings, compelling grounds now exist for a 50 basis points cut," said John Edwards, chief economist at Societe Generale.
The benchmark November 2006 10-year bond yield fell below 7.40 percent, over 35 basis points down from its most recent high just a week ago, and looks destined to go even lower.
The view from offshore was equally bullish.
"Further (price) gains are anticipated," said Jane Berryman, fixed income analysts at Technical Data in Tokyo.
"When you have an all clear on the price pressures front, that's definitely a recipe for a bull run north. So we expect the market to press higher," Berryman added.
December bill futures fully priced in a 50 basis points cut, spiking to 93.55 and indicating a cash rate of 6.45 percent. The RBA last eased policy on July 31 to 7.0 percent from 7.5.

The December 10-year bond futures finally cracked resistance at 92.560 and touched a high of 92.645 after news that August quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) rose just 0.7 percent against an expected 1.0 percent increase.
This followed Wednesday's fall in annual underlying inflation to 2.4 percent and well within the RBA's target range.
However, technically, bond futures could be due for a short-term correction given the extent of the current rally.
"The market has over stretched itself and is due for a correction to around the 92.350/400 region," said Mark Power, technical analyst at MMS International.

"(But) the trend is obviously very clearly up an I think we are going to be looking at considerably lower yields at the 10-year end of the curve," Power added, citing a level of 93.000 in the next six to seven trading weeks.
